page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8488C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz. The instance provisions 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing symmetric multithreading with 2 threads per core under a burstable CPU allocation model. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance contains no bundled local storage and requires remote network-attached volumes. Networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no dedicated GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results indicate mid-tier execution capabilities across general compute suites alongside specific instruction-level strengths. Single-core performance falls within average ranges, recording 1892.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1880.68 in stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core compute yields average to lower-tier results, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 4435.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 7332.31, while stress-ng multi-core registers at 3944.96. The instance achieves strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.91 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2498.0. Conversely, memory subsystem benchmarks show constrained throughput, recording 26.17 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 299.52 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read tests. Database operations under PassMark register at 2063.13 and Redis SET operations attain 5.08 million operations per second, both scoring in lower benchmark tiers.

As part of the flex tier, this instance trades continuous sustained compute capacity for cost-effective execution in workloads with variable CPU utilization. The absence of local NVMe storage requires dependence on external block storage, which can introduce I/O latency in storage-heavy environments. The inclusion of AMX hardware extensions enables small-scale machine learning inference, demonstrated by 107.91 tokens per second on text generation with a 135M model, though larger models exhibit clear memory and bandwidth bottlenecks. Static web serving reaches a solid throughput of 7.35 GB/sec. This configuration is best suited for general web serving, light application backends, text processing pipelines, and staging environments where peak computational demands occur intermittently.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance offering 4 burstable vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor using the x86_64 architecture, it includes 16 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz and provides a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance features no local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without GPUs. The processor incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks indicate average single-core and multi-core CPU capacity, highlighted by strong performance in gzip compression and text processing, but lower throughput in memory-bound tasks and database transactions. Its burstable configuration delivers resource efficiency for workloads with fluctuating utilization, making it suited for static web serving, microservices, light data parsing, and general application hosting.
